messages.subject: cluster using generated quantities
parts:
Dears Rstan users,

I run my model where 2-gaussian mixture model.
I've data PxQ transformed in vector of length N=P*Q.
So I have for each column two means, a total of 2 means per columns.

My model is OK when I just estimate mean, lambda and sigma. 

Now my question is how can I complete my model using generated quantities to categorize each individu in each column in its group (0 or 1).

data {
  int Q; // nombre d'items
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1,upper=Q> qq[N]; 
  int<lower=1> K;
  real y[N];
}

parameters {
real<lower=0,upper=1> lambda[Q];
real<lower=0> beta[Q];
real mu1[Q];
matrix<lower=0>[K,Q] sigma;
} 

transformed parameters {
real mu2[Q];
  for(q in 1:Q){
    mu2[q] = mu1[q]+beta[q];
  }
  
} 

model {
  to_vector(sigma) ~ cauchy(0, 2.5);
  mu1 ~ normal(0, 100);
  beta ~ normal(0,100);
  for (n in 1:N) {
    target += log_mix(lambda[qq[n]],
    normal_lpdf(y[n] | mu1[qq[n]], sigma[1,qq[n]]),
    normal_lpdf(y[n] | mu2[qq[n]], sigma[2,qq[n]]));
  }
}

generated quantities{
  int<lower=0,upper=1> z[N];
  
  for(n in 1:N){
    
  }

}

Bests regards

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] cluster using generated quantities
parts:
Woo hoo! An easy one. lambda is your mixing proportion. So...

  for(n in 1:N){
    z[n] = bernoulli_rng(lambda[qq[n]]);
  }

(I didn't check to see if that compiles, but it should be close.)



Daniel

parts:
Hi Daniel,

Thank you for your prompt response. However, lambda is the proportion of mixing for each column. So to obtain the percentage of each assignment, I need using data and different mean. Is it correct ?

data {
  int Q; // nombre d'items
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1,upper=Q> qq[N]; 
  int<lower=1> K;
  real y[N];
}

parameters {
real<lower=0,upper=1> lambda[Q];
real<lower=0> beta[Q];
real mu1[Q];
matrix<lower=0>[K,Q] sigma;
} 

transformed parameters {
real mu2[Q];
vector[2] lp_parts[N];

for(q in 1:Q){
    mu2[q] = mu1[q]+beta[q];
  }

// New Script Add
  for(n in 1:N){
    lp_parts[n,1] = log(lambda[qq[n]]) + normal_lpdf(y[n] | mu1[qq[n]],sigma[1,qq[n]]);
    lp_parts[n,2] = log1m(lambda[qq[n]]) + normal_lpdf(y[n] | mu2[qq[n]],sigma[2,qq[n]]);

}
} 

model {
  to_vector(sigma) ~ cauchy(0, 2.5);
  mu1 ~ normal(0, 100);
  beta ~ normal(0,100);
  for (n in 1:N) {
    target += log_mix(lambda[qq[n]],
    normal_lpdf(y[n] | mu1[qq[n]], sigma[1,qq[n]]),
    normal_lpdf(y[n] | mu2[qq[n]], sigma[2,qq[n]]));
  }
}
// New Script Add

generated quantities{
  int<lower=0,upper=1> z[N];
  
  for(n in 1:N){

vector[2] prob;
    prob = softmax(lp_parts[n]);
    z[n] = bernoulli_rng(prob[1]);
  }
}

Bests regards
